problem_framing: Problem: a single Thai merchant has no direct online sales channel and today leans on phone/chat to sell; it wants customers to self-serve the entire purchase journey (browse -> cart -> checkout -> mock payment -> delivery tracking) while back-office staff run catalog, stock, orders and coupons from one console. For whom: B2C retail customers in Thailand (guest and registered) and the merchant's own back-office staff; own-data-only isolation between customers is treated as non-negotiable. Why now: this is the merchant's first online storefront and, equally, the squad's vehicle to validate an end-to-end software-delivery workflow on a 'small but complete' MVP (single merchant, single currency/language, mock payment and shipping) that must nonetheless 'actually sell' -- stock reservation, server-computed totals, coupon rules and pre-shipment cancellation genuinely enforced -- and stay extensible to a real payment provider, real shipping and a future loyalty/points program without a rebuild. PROVENANCE / RB-01: the source ecommerce_mvp_business_only.gap-closed.md is already a fully-structured requirement (sections 1-20: RACI, PII inventory, retention schedule, quantified SLOs), which is exactly this skill's RB-01 'input already a structured requirement -> route to intake' condition. Per explicit instruction this discovery is produced retrospectively -- framing the opportunity from the business narrative (sections 1-3) and the resolved regulatory context (section 18) rather than from a raw, pre-intake idea -- so it reads as a derived problem-space record, not true upstream discovery. AI drafts; the named human decides at the review gate, then hands the framing into intake (eliciting-banking-brief), which is materialized here as the brief + epics + stories layers of this S1 pack.
opportunities: Direct self-serve online sales channel: let customers complete a purchase end-to-end on the web without phone or chat, lifting the registration->first-purchase and checkout->payment conversion the business wants to measure.
Unified back-office console: let merchant staff manage catalog, inventory, orders, fulfillment state and coupons in one place, cutting operational handling time and same-day fulfillment lag.

A trustworthy 'it actually sells' MVP: correct stock reservation, server-computed totals, idempotent confirm/payment and audited state changes so customers never hit overselling or double charges (the zero-defect quality KPIs).
An extensible foundation: a structure that admits a real payment provider, a real shipping provider and a future loyalty/points program without re-architecting.
An end-to-end SDLC workflow testbed: use ShopPilot as the reference initiative to exercise the squad's delivery pipeline from discovery through deployment.

assumptions.statement: Thai B2C shoppers will complete purchases unassisted on a single-merchant web storefront rather than reverting to phone/chat ordering.
assumptions.de_risk: Instrument the registration->first-purchase and checkout->payment funnels (section 3) and read them post-launch; run 5-8 customer interviews or a demand test before committing later-phase investment.

assumptions.statement: Guest, customer and admin can each complete their core flows (browse->pay; manage catalog/stock/orders) without training, including the own-data-only rule and applying a coupon at checkout.
assumptions.de_risk: Moderated prototype usability tests on the checkout and admin-fulfillment flows; verify the section 20 accessibility targets (keyboard-usable, responsive, human-readable error/confirmation messages).

assumptions.statement: Mock payment/shipping plus atomic stock reservation with a 30-minute TTL, last-item-race resolution, idempotent confirm and provider-replay-safe callbacks, and price snapshots can be built and hardened within the one-sprint budget (section 7.1).
assumptions.de_risk: Run a time-boxed spike on the reservation + idempotency concurrency model (last-item race and provider-replay dedup) before commit, and hand the spike to a technical-feasibility assessment.

assumptions.statement: A single-merchant MVP is sustainable for the business and the regulator: PDPA obligations (per-field lawful basis, TH/SG residency, 5-year retention), CPA/ETA disclosure and a PCI-out-of-scope payment model are operable at this scale.
assumptions.de_risk: Largely de-risked in the gap-closed governance workshop (sections 14-20: named Legal/DPO/Compliance owners, resolved citations); keep a cost model and confirm the manual-refund SOP (refunds over 3,000 THB need dual approval) is operationally staffed.

regulatory_regimes: PDPA B.E. 2562 (2019): per-field lawful basis (section 15), data-subject access/correction/erasure via a back-office request, separate marketing-email consent, and a defined breach-notification path; lawful basis resolved.
Data residency: all personal data confined to the Thailand/Singapore (ap-southeast) region (section 16).
Revenue Code: 5-year retention envelope for order, financial and audit records (section 16).
Consumer Protection Act and Electronic Transactions Act: price and total shown before payment; order confirmation treated as an electronic record (section 18).
PCI-DSS v4.0: ShopPilot stays out of cardholder-data scope -- no PAN/CVV collected or stored; mock provider now, PSP tokenization later (section 18).

Not in play: KYC / AML / sanctions screening -- there is no account opening, lending, or money movement beyond tokenized retail payment; flagged explicitly so intake does not assume a financial-crime regime. No hard regulatory blocker remains (all section 18 citations resolved).
